test_vectors.coverage: HTTPServerID has exact expected outputs under all six NameCase variants.

Seventeen vectors across five conversion cases cover single letters and digits, uppercase runs, acronym boundaries, lowercase-to-uppercase boundaries, digit-to-uppercase boundaries, and digits retained within words.
Underscore, hyphen, space, TAB, LF, CR, and form feed, including repeated, leading, trailing, and mixed separators.
Empty input fails every case; separator-only inputs fail conversions and survive Preserve unchanged.
Unicode, combining marks, emoji, punctuation, NUL, DEL, whitespace, and canonically equivalent but byte-distinct strings remain exact.
Every conversion rejects non-ASCII letters, combining marks, emoji, nonbreaking space, and em space with canonical error metadata.
All 128 ASCII bytes in interior positions under every case, with explicit allowed ranges and rejection of punctuation and unsupported controls.
65536-byte names under every policy and 1024 repeated acronym-containing segments.
Frozen defaults, empty lists under all twelve policy combinations, and exact preservation of ASCII and Unicode sources.
Unsorted declaration order, exact source retention, expected snake outputs, source immutability, and independent owned results after source mutation.
Nonadjacent duplicate sources fail with DuplicateObjectKey under all twelve policies without mutating input.
Acronym, separator, whitespace, and digit collisions in every conversion policy, plus camel and Pascal collisions caused by separator removal.
Case-sensitive Preserve permits distinct ASCII spellings; case-insensitive Preserve rejects them; Pascal results retain emitted casing.
Prefixes, punctuation, Unicode case distinctions, combining marks, and embedded NUL; ASCII letters are folded even within Unicode and NUL-containing strings.
Invalid and empty sources across every policy propagate ConstraintViolation and retain the original source list.
An earlier duplicate takes precedence over a later invalid name; an earlier invalid name takes precedence over a later duplicate; repeated failures are deterministic.
Valid letter, underscore, digit-tail, acronym, and mixed-case identifiers, exact case distinctions, and 65536-byte components.
Empty and lone-underscore components, digit starts, dots, punctuation, surrounding whitespace, controls, Unicode, and invalid service precedence.
All 128 ASCII bytes in leading and trailing positions for both service and endpoint components, including the lone-underscore exception.
A valid boundary-ID model resolves the same borrowed endpoint by the emitted method key; recased and dotted alternatives miss.
